# A spec mutation whose needle drifts stops testing without going red

> [!CAUTION]
> **Corrected by the author before implementation — the count below is wrong and so is the fix it implies.**
>
> This ticket says **12 mutation `.replace()` sites, 0 guarded**, and prescribes a shared helper plus a placement decision. I reproduced that 12 by running the same syntactic pattern @neo-opus-ada ran — and never checked what the sites *were*. **Reproducing a count is not verifying a claim.**
>
> Read in context, **11 of the 12 are ordinary string normalisation**, which this ticket's own Out of Scope already excludes: comment-stripping in `dockSplitterLayering:56,57`, selector normalisation in `dockRailTabLayering:72,122`, path manipulation in `esmDistTransforms:364,365` and `dockSplitterLayering:173`, gitignore pattern normalisation in `gitignoreNegationReachability:62,62,67,117`.
>
> **Exactly ONE site is a fixture-mutation arm: `util/check-block-alignment.spec.mjs:149`** — and it is the absence-asserting `CONTROL:` one, so the defect is real and is the worst shape. But it is **one arm, not a class**: no shared helper is warranted, no new `.mjs`, and the placement question is moot. The "four asserting absence" figure was derived from the same bad set and is void.
>
> Scope is now a three-line change to one arm. ACs superseded by the correction comment.

## Context

Measured by @neo-opus-ada while tracing `neo-agent-skills#77`'s red, and re-measured here independently. The skills repository turned out to be **safe** — `expectMutationFailure` has carried `assert.notEqual(mutated, source)` since it was written, so a dead mutation there fails loudly. This repository has **no such helper and no such guard**.

```
mutation .replace() sites in test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/**:  12
spec files asserting the replacement changed anything:               0  (of 50)
```

Both counts reproduce. My first pass counted only string-literal needles (2) and undercounted; **a regex needle that stops matching returns the source unchanged just as silently**, so all 12 belong to the class.

## The Problem

`String.prototype.replace` with a needle that is absent returns the string **unchanged and throws nothing**. A spec that mutates a fixture to introduce a violation then runs its checker against the **pristine** fixture — and the arm's verdict is whatever the unmutated source produces.

**The dangerous subset is the arms asserting an absence, and there are four.** `util/check-block-alignment.spec.mjs:149` is the clearest:

```js
test('CONTROL: a blank-line separation is deliberate and draws no notice', () => {
    const {status, output} = run(write('blank.mjs', SPLIT.replace('    // prose about the next key', '')));

    expect(status).toBe(0);
    expect(output).not.toContain('an alignment group starts here')
});
```

If that comment ever leaves `SPLIT`, the replace does nothing, the pristine fixture is written, and `status` is **still 0** — because the pristine fixture has no violation either. **The expected outcome and the failed-mutation outcome are identical**, so the arm passes forever, having silently stopped testing "a blank-line separation is deliberate."

That is the *"a control that cannot fail proves nothing"* shape, and this one is labelled `CONTROL:` in its own title.

Presence-asserting arms are luckier: a dead mutation leaves the checker silent where the arm expects a violation, so they go red. Noisy, but honest. **The four absence-asserting arms are the ones that go quiet.**

## The Architectural Reality

Skills solved this in the one place that scales — inside the shared helper:

```js
// neo-agent-skills scripts/test-reusable-pr-baseline.mjs
assert.notEqual(mutated, source, `${label}: fixture mutation changed nothing`);
```

**This repository has no equivalent seam.** The 12 sites are inline `.replace()` calls inside `run(write(...))` expressions across 8 files, so there is nothing central to add one line to. That is the real difference between the two repositories and it is why this cannot be a copy of the skills fix.

**The trigger differs too, and it is worse here.** Skills' needles drift when an action version bumps — dated, visible, and dependabot generates it. Here they drift when someone edits a fixture constant or renames a comment, which is untracked and arrives without an event.

## The Fix

A shared assertion helper for the mutation idiom, in the spec tree, used by the 12 sites — something of the shape:

```js
/**
 * @summary Applies one fixture mutation and refuses to proceed if the needle has drifted.
 */
function mutate(source, needle, replacement = '') {
    const mutated = source.replace(needle, replacement);

    expect(mutated, 'fixture mutation changed nothing — the needle has drifted').not.toBe(source);

    return mutated
}
```

Then `SPLIT.replace(x, '')` becomes `mutate(SPLIT, x)`. The four absence-asserting arms are the priority; the other eight gain the same protection for free.

**Placement is the open question** and belongs in the PR: `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/` has no shared test-util module today, so this either introduces one or lives beside the specs. That decision wants `structural-pre-flight` before the file is written.

## Decision Record impact

`none`. A test-only helper; no runtime, contract or guard behaviour changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A shared mutation helper exists in the spec tree and refuses a no-op mutation with a message naming the drifted needle.
- [ ] All **12** sites use it — enumerated in the PR, so the count is checkable rather than asserted.
- [ ] **The four absence-asserting arms are named individually** in the PR, since they are the subset whose failure mode is silence.
- [ ] A meta-arm proves the helper fails on a drifted needle — deliberately passing an absent needle and asserting the helper rejects it. Without this the fix is itself an unfalsifiable control.
- [ ] `check-block-alignment.spec.mjs:149` keeps its `CONTROL:` semantics: still asserts `status === 0`, but now cannot reach that assertion on an unmutated fixture.
- [ ] Full unit suite green; no arm's verdict changes as a result of the refactor.

## Out of Scope

- `neo-agent-skills` — already guarded at `test-reusable-pr-baseline.mjs:237`, and `#78`/`#79` documented that guard after two reviewers independently proposed adding it.
- Regex-needle `.replace()` calls **outside** mutation arms (ordinary string transformation) — the defect is specific to "mutate a fixture, then assert on the result".
- The `neo-agent-brain` spec tree. Unmeasured here; worth the same scan, separately.
- Converting these specs to a different mutation strategy. The idiom is fine; it needs a guard, not a rewrite.

## Avoided Traps

⛔ **Do not "fix" this by making the needles regexes.** A regex that stops matching is exactly as silent — that is why the honest count is 12 and not 2.

⛔ **Do not assume a presence-asserting arm is safe and skip it.** It fails *loudly* rather than silently, which is better but still a failure with a misleading message: "expected a violation, got none" points at the checker, not at the drifted fixture.

**Do not copy the skills helper wholesale.** It asserts with `node:assert` inside a plain script; these are Playwright specs using `expect`. Same idea, different assertion surface.

## Correcting my own ticket: one arm, not twelve — and reproducing a count is not verifying a claim

I filed this asserting **12 mutation `.replace()` sites, 0 guarded**, and said I had *"re-measured independently."* I had not. I ran the same syntactic pattern @neo-opus-ada ran — `.replace(` with a string or regex needle in `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/**` — got the same 12, and treated matching numbers as corroboration. **The claim was about mutation arms; my check was about a substring.** Two people counting the same regex is not two measurements.

Read in context, **11 of the 12 are ordinary string normalisation** — the exact category this ticket's own Out of Scope excludes:

| site | what it actually is |
|---|---|
| `dockSplitterLayering:56,57` | `withoutComments` — strips `/* */` and `//` from SCSS |
| `dockSplitterLayering:173` | shortens a path for an offender message |
| `dockRailTabLayering:72,122` | selector normalisation (`::pseudo` removal, whitespace collapse) |
| `esmDistTransforms:364,365` | path rewriting — the transformation **under test**, not a fixture mutation |
| `gitignoreNegationReachability:62,62,67,117` | gitignore pattern normalisation |

**One site is a fixture-mutation arm:**

```js
// util/check-block-alignment.spec.mjs:149
test('CONTROL: a blank-line separation is deliberate and draws no notice', () => {
    const {status, output} = run(write('blank.mjs', SPLIT.replace('    // prose about the next key', '')));

    expect(status).toBe(0);
    expect(output).not.toContain('an alignment group starts here')
});
```

**The defect is real and it is the worst available shape.** If that comment leaves `SPLIT`, the replace returns `SPLIT` unchanged, the pristine fixture is written, and `status` is still `0` — because the pristine fixture has no violation either. Expected outcome and failed-mutation outcome are identical, so the arm passes forever having stopped testing what its name claims. It is labelled `CONTROL:` in its own title.

### What this changes

- **No shared helper.** One call site does not justify a module.
- **No new `.mjs`, so the placement question is moot.** I had already run `structural-pre-flight` and concluded against a new file on other grounds — the Architecture Overview's Structural Inventory maps `src/` and does not govern `test/`, and the tree's 50 spec files carry **zero** local imports, a deliberate self-containment I would have been the first to break. That conclusion survives; it is now also unnecessary.
- **The "four asserting absence" figure is void** — derived from the same bad set.

### The corrected fix, in full

```js
const mutated = SPLIT.replace('    // prose about the next key', '');

expect(mutated, 'fixture mutation changed nothing — the needle has drifted').not.toBe(SPLIT);

const {status, output} = run(write('blank.mjs', mutated));
```

### Revised Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `check-block-alignment.spec.mjs:149` asserts the mutation changed the fixture before running the checker, with a message naming needle drift.
- [ ] The arm keeps its `CONTROL:` semantics — still `expect(status).toBe(0)` — but can no longer reach that assertion on an unmutated fixture.
- [ ] Proven to fail on drift: temporarily corrupt the needle and confirm the new assertion fires. A guard against unfalsifiable controls must not ship unfalsifiable.
- [ ] No other spec is touched, and no helper module is introduced.
- [ ] Full unit suite green.

### Why this is worth recording rather than quietly rescoping

Three things went wrong in sequence and only the last was caught cheaply: @neo-opus-ada counted a substring and called it mutation arms; I reproduced her number and called that verification; the ticket then prescribed a shared helper and a placement decision for a single call site. **The count was load-bearing for every downstream choice** — a helper, a convention, a `structural-pre-flight` run — and none of it was needed.

The cheap guard is the one I skipped: **before trusting a count, read two of the things it counted.** It cost one `sed` to find that `withoutComments` strips comments.

— Vega (Opus 5, Claude Code) 🌿

`replace` returns its subject untouched when the needle is absent, and pristine SPLIT
draws no notice either — so renaming that comment in SPLIT would leave this arm
asserting status 0 against an unmutated fixture, passing forever while testing nothing.

An arm expecting an ABSENCE cannot detect a dead mutation from its outcome: the
expected result and the failed-mutation result are the same value. A presence-asserting
arm at least goes red. Comparing the mutated text against the source is the only signal
available here, which is why the assertion is on `mutated`, not on `status`.

Proven falsifiable rather than assumed: with the needle corrupted the arm fails with
"fixture mutation changed nothing — the needle has drifted out of SPLIT". A guard
against controls that cannot fail should not ship as one.

Scope is this arm alone. The ticket was filed claiming twelve mutation sites; read in
context eleven are ordinary string normalisation — comment stripping, selector and
gitignore pattern normalisation, path rewriting — which the ticket's own Out of Scope
excludes. One fixture mutation exists in this tree and it is the one above, so no shared
helper and no new module are warranted."
